reason: No examiner or auditor has asked us how we control customers' AI agents, so this would never get through my risk committee as a priority this year. Even the free pilot costs me staff time and a letter of intent with a price in it, and I'm not signing that for a problem nobody is asking me about.
objection: It's a pre-revenue startup with no SOC 2 and no customers sitting inline in front of every trade and payment. Vendor due diligence alone would kill it, and if it goes down or goes under I have a gate in my order path that nobody can vouch for.
would_change_my_mind: FINRA or the SEC putting AI agent supervision into exam priorities or a regulatory notice, or an examiner asking us directly for evidence of how agent trades are authorized and supervised.
